subject: Re: MAP kickoff + staggered rebate request
messages:
From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@accel.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@accel.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft + pilot rebate ask

Tessa / Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We went through the technical evaluation internally and there’s strong alignment on Redwood for inference at scale. We’d like to move to a 3-month pilot followed by a 12-month committed ramp if the pilot hits the KPIs in the MAP (attached).

Ask: to make the pilot economics work for our procurement committee, can Redwood support a staged rebate: 25% credit on invoices for months 1–3 (pilot), stepping down to 10% for months 4–6, with MAC (minimum annual commitment) of $225k ARR in month 12? We understand this is a rebate tied to milestones (pilot KPIs + integration checkpoint) and open to structure as credits or true-up at renewal.

Attached: AccelAI_MAP_v0.9.pdf — draft with milestone dates and KPI targets.

We’re targeting production evaluation start 10/01 and legal prefers a single DocuSign for MAP + SOW once commercial terms are finalized.

Jordan
Jordan Mills
Head of Platform Partnerships, AccelAI
jordan.mills@accel.ai
+1 415 555 0192

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft + pilot rebate ask

Looping you in — Jordan’s asking for a staged rebate (25% -> 10%) tied to MAP milestones with a $225k ARR commit by month 12. They want credits applied against invoices during the ramp and a single DocuSign for MAP+SOW.

Proposed commercial alternative (to reduce near-term margin impact):
- Offer 15% credit for months 1–3 (pilot) if pilot KPIs met; 7.5% months 4–6.
- Provide a $40k implementation credit (one-time) contingent on deployment by 11/15.
- True-up at renewal if they hit $225k ARR — additional discretionary rebate up to 5% applied retroactively.

Why: reduces short-term subsidy while showing commitment. They’ve signaled tight procurement timelines — want DocuSign by 9/30.

Neha / Marissa — can we get a margin/finance read from Rishi? If we need exec sign-off we should flag now (I think >$50k quarterly subsidy will climb above our VP threshold).

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive — West
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the context — quick finance take: at Ben’s proposed structure the up-front cash subsidy (credits + implementation credit) would be ~ $55k over the first 6 months assuming their projected usage profile. If they deliver on $225k ARR at month 12 and we true-up, the NPV looks reasonable, but we need: 

1) A simple margin / cashflow model from Ben showing expected monthly invoice run-rate under pilot and ramp (month 1–12).
2) Confirmation whether credits are invoiced as negative line items (affects revenue recognition) or recorded as contra revenue (affects gross margin).
3) Legal input on whether the rebate must be escrowed/held for clawback if KPIs fail.

Given size of the subsidy, this needs VP Sales approval and CFO sign-off for any credit > $50k. If we’re above $75k we’ll need CEO awareness/exec approval. Can you get Ben to push a conservative usage projection and we’ll run the numbers today.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Rishi — quick projection attached (spreadsheet summarized in the doc below). Conservative plan assumes slow pilot ramp: $15k/mo month 1, $25k/mo month 2, $45k/mo month 3, then linear ramp to $225k ARR by month 12. Under my alternative structure the expected credit exposure is ~$48k over months 1–6 (implementation credit included).

Summary:
- Pilot start: 2026-10-01
- Proposed credits: 15% months 1–3, 7.5% months 4–6; $40k implementation credit on go-live by 11/15.
- True-up: if ARR >= $225k by month 12, we apply an additional retrospective rebate up to 5% (discretionary).
- Contractual form: credits applied as invoice line items; legal to confirm whether contra revenue preferred.

Ben
